baseline.integratorAssessment: programmer-art tier (~5): fallback serif fonts, debug vectors on by default, flat circles for asteroids, touch pads always visible on desktop, flat rectangles for lunar surface and pad, painted 1280px planets mismatched with pixel ship, no audio.

strengths: Massive improvement over the baseline: every placeholder grey circle and debug overlay is gone, and all art loads with zero fallbacks.
Palette is on-brand: cosmos #17182D base, plum nebula, sage/cream Tea Moon, amber/orange accents that match design-system tokens.
Asteroid cast has real personality (sleepy face, mossy tea rock, mochi, rice). They feel cozy and handcrafted, not hazardous-generic.
Tea Moon destination is a genuine hero moment: the teacup crater, tiny tea house with steam and soft stepped halo read instantly as 'deliver here'.

Huge leap from baseline: no debug HUD, no vector placeholder circles, and no fallback textures. The palette (navy cosmos, cream, orange accent, sage/plum) matches colors_and_type.css and design-system tokens.
Hero ship now renders crisp at an integer 2x when axis-aligned (flight-start/cruise). The round-1 0.72 non-integer smear is fixed.
Asteroids are characterful, consistently 2x pixel art with good silhouettes and cozy faces. Planets are now opaque, so the round-1 ghosting is fixed.

Tea Moon destination is a strong focal point: cottage, smoke, teacup crater, stepped halo. The gate language (dashed orange ring, then a cream progress arc over sage dashes, a chevron, a status chip) reads clearly.

Both round-2 majors are fixed. The compact phone HUD keeps the bottom heading and package rows, and on touch the gate pill now sits above the gate, clear of the brake/thrust pads (r3-critic-flight-touch/flight-arrival-ready@phoneLandscapeTouch.png).
Parallax depth now reads. Far planets are hazed and desaturated, with nebula clouds in front of them, and foreground asteroids keep crisp ink outlines and full saturation.
The RotSprite pre-rotated ship removed the jagged nearest-neighbour rotation. The crust and dome outlines are clean at 90, 107 and 270 degrees.
The nebula is now authored stepped pixel cloud banks instead of upscaled mush. Its density matches the stars and asteroids.

openIssues: [minor] (flight) The arrival gate ring overlaps the moon's face. Its dashes and the cream progress arc cut across the lit hemisphere and through the teacup crater, the scene's signature detail, so the hero landmark is partly drawn over at the key payoff moment.

[minor] (flight) The moon's glow halo reads as a muddy grey disc rather than warm light. The stepped bands darken the nebula behind the moon into a grey annulus, which flattens the focal point. This is the same 'grey halo' problem the ui critic flagged on the title.

[minor] (ui) The HUD panel is translucent enough that world objects (a pebble asteroid, the nebula, the edge of the ringed planet) show through behind the readout rows. A dark pebble sits right between 'bottom' and '269°' on phone, which muddies the core readout.

[minor] (flight) The ship's side-view silhouette still reads as a croissant or bagel more than a gyoza, and it is small (about 60 px long on desktop) next to the 80-200 px asteroids and planets. The hatched ghost target is a wide saucer that does not match the narrow crescent the player flies, so the 'match this pose' cue is less direct.
[nit] (audio-fx) The cruise thrust trail breaks into evenly spaced orange beads followed by cream puffs, so it reads like a string of sausages rather than a dissipating exhaust.

[nit] (flight) A small pink pebble asteroid lands exactly on top of Planet I'm Fine's bandage, the planet's joke detail. The 'bottom to moon' pill in playtest step 03 renders very faint, probably mid-fade, so the label is barely legible in that frame.

strengths: Huge visual leap over baseline: cohesive dusk palette (plum/navy sky, peach planet, cream ground, terracotta/sage accents) that matches colors_and_type.css warmth
Diegetic landing site: striped blanket on trestles, lanterns that light sequentially on touchdown, cottage with chimney smoke, rabbit NPC who waves on soft landing - strong cozy storytelling
Copy voice is on-brand: lowercase, warm, funny low-stakes failure lines ('moon blanket says: softer, please', 'Emotionally rotated')
Parchment result card with state dot + retry progress bar reads clearly on desktop and matches the UI kit
Huge leap over the baseline: a full handcrafted Tea Moon diorama (sky gradient, hills, banded planet, steaming cottage, waving rabbit, lanterns, striped blanket pad) on one consistent 2 px pixel grid
Upright ship redraw at 64x80@2x is crisp, readable and charming; it matches the pixel density of the scenery
HUD follows the design system: dark 0.78 panel, pixel-font gold header, mono rows, ember/amber state colouring, gentle flavour copy ('emotionally rotated', 'slightly shaken')
Live speed gauge with soft/bumpy/too-fast bands and a state pill gives clear, cozy landing feedback
The RotSprite pre-rotated ship removes the jagged rotation. The tilted, tipped and off-pad poses keep a clean ink outline and dome ring.
The HUD now agrees with the world state after an incident and off the pad (tipped over, bounced/stopped, off blanket).
Soft-landing dust fans out sideways and leaves the saucer, legs and dome readable at the payoff moment. The sparkle accents above the ship are a nice touch.
The guide beam was reworked into subtle stepped light bands with a dotted descent line. It no longer reads as placeholder rectangles.

openIssues: [minor] (audio-fx) The lantern halos that light up on a successful landing are smooth, anti-aliased radial gradients: soft pink discs with continuous alpha falloff. They sit beside crisp pixel lanterns. This is the same defect class as the round-2 engine glow major, now moved to the success moment.

[minor] (landing) The compact phone landing HUD drops tilt, drift and altitude, and it drops the dashboard chatter line entirely. ui-reference 'Flight HUD' lists the dashboard line as essential live data. Tilt is the core landing verb, but on phone the only tilt feedback is the sprite itself.

[minor] (landing) On touch, the control pads sit inside the 16:9 game area while both pillarbox bars stay empty. The 'steady' pad covers the teahouse's right wall and the planet ring. The velocity gauge's 'soft' chip touches the rabbit. The scene's focal props compete with the controls.

[minor] (audio-fx) The incident flour still forms a vertical cream column rising from the pad through the tumbling ship. Some confetti crosses sit flat on the blanket at pad level, so the comedic poof stays somewhat muddled under the ship.
[nit] (landing) The HUD tilt row reads 'level 6°' while the ship is visibly tilted in the thrust capture (and 'level 0°' during descent). Calling a visible lean 'level' undercuts the feedback.

[nit] (audio-fx) In the thrust state, one cream trail puff hangs detached in mid-air about 40 px above the pad, between the flame and the ground dust. It reads as a stray cloud instead of part of the exhaust.
[nit] (landing) The incident view offers only 'R retry' (or the touch RETRY button). ui-reference 'Crash And Respawn' also asks for an option to return to the map.

strengths: Huge improvement over the baseline title: a cohesive warm-cosmos palette that matches colors_and_type.css (terracotta, sage, cream parchment, cosmos ink)
Strong typographic hierarchy: Bricolage 800 two-tone title with a warm offset shadow, a clear subtitle, and a distinct Silkscreen CTA
The parchment delivery card reads as handcrafted stationery: dotted divider, corner ticks, portrait, item tile, gentle pill. It balances well against the dominant cosmos.
Saved completion is clearly visible on title-completed: tape sticker, sage 'delivered' pill and a happy portrait swap

A real typographic hierarchy: Bricolage 800 display title with a two-tone cream/ember lockup and terracotta offset shadow, then a Bricolage tagline, Silkscreen pixel labels on buttons and section heads, mono for keycaps and data. Fonts load with no failures and the hierarchy matches design-system.md.

Parchment and cosmos are well balanced. One warm card and one ember CTA anchor a deep-cosmos field with pixel clouds, and the tea-cup moon, teahouse and dotted route trail tell the delivery story at a glance.

Saved completion is clearly visible on title-completed: CTA copy changes to 'deliver tea again', a Route Log button appears, a 'delivered · postcard collected' tab and 'delivered' pill show, and the rabbit portrait becomes happy. The Route Log modal shows the collected postcard and stats.
Corrupt-save handling is friendly and on-tone ('your old save was crumpled...'), and the probe confirms the backup was kept.
The hero ship is now about 150 px wide at desktop, inside the 140-180 px design target. It has crisp pixel edges and the grey halo is gone. It reads as the star of the screen.
The secondary buttons on the title are now consistent: SETTINGS and ROUTE LOG share the same navy treatment and lip, with clear hierarchy under the ember primary.
Saved completion is visible at a glance: the 'DELIVER TEA AGAIN' CTA, the ROUTE LOG button, an integrated '✓ postcard collected' tab and a 'delivered' state pill.

Typography has a clear three-voice system: Bricolage 800 display, Bricolage 600 heading, a mono body and Silkscreen pixel labels. Letter-spacing is consistent and contrast is strong on both navy and parchment.

openIssues: [minor] (ui) The completed-state card still says the delivery is pending. It keeps the 'TODAY'S DELIVERY' header and the present-tense request ('Someone needs tea before the stars get too loud.'), while also showing two overlapping completion badges ('✓ postcard collected' plus a 'delivered' pill). The earned postcard art never appears on the title, so the payoff is told, not shown.

[minor] (ui) The ui-kit button matrix still includes a cream 'ROUTE LOG' secondary variant that the title no longer uses (it now uses navy). Two different 'PRESSED' looks also sit side by side without variant labels. As a component reference it documents a style the product has dropped, which invites the round-2 inconsistency back.

[minor] (ui) Small text at phone size. On ui-kit@phoneLandscape the section subtitles, the '↑ held' legend, the meter labels and percentages, and the HUD stat labels render at about 6-7 px. On title@phoneLandscape the keycap legends 'start' and 'sound' are about 9 px, below a comfortable minimum for a handheld screen.

[nit] (ui) phoneLandscape title is vertically unbalanced. The delivery card's bottom border sits about 10 px from the canvas bottom while the title block has about 25 px top margin, so the card looks like it is sliding off-screen. The footer is also dropped.

[nit] (ui) Meter fractional segments use one fixed dim tint whatever the fraction. 18% (1.8 segments) and 72% (7.2 segments) both show an identical dim trailing block, so 18% reads like about 15% and 72% like 75%.

[nit] (ui) The footer 'handmade slice · ofl type' is low-contrast and uses dev-speak on the player-facing title. Separately, the dotted flight path to the moon starts in empty space about 30 px from the ship instead of trailing from it.

strengths: Audio engine is architecturally excellent: a pure, exhaustive GameEvent mapper (audioCues.ts) separated from Web Audio rendering, all tuning in typed data, and a unit-test file present (tests/audioCues.test.ts).

Gesture-gated AudioContext verified live: 'uncreated' before input, 'running' after a pointer click. Keydown, pointerdown and touchend all unlock. The context suspends and resumes with tab visibility.

Robust mastering chain (glue compressor, then limiter, then tanh soft-clip at -1 dBFS). Offline analysis shows the stacked worst case (result music + thrust + dramatic bump + incident + touchdown + chime) peaking at only -3.6 dBFS, with no clipping and no NaNs.
Graceful failure everywhere: handleEvent, the scheduler, loops and sfx are all try/catch-wrapped, there is a webkit fallback, and nothing runs (silent no-op) until a gesture unlocks the context.
Round-1 FX majors resolved: the landing nozzle flame is now pixel tongue frames at integer 2x, with no anti-aliased triangle or banded radial disc
Particle pixel density now matches the 2x ship and scenery, and particles pop out fully opaque, with no grey alpha mush over navy
Dust no longer shows charcoal tail frames. Cream, gold and ember palette is warm and cohesive with the Tea Moon art
Flight bump feedback reads well: hard tint flash on ship and rock, then a cream puff bloom between them
The round-2 major is fixed: the flight engine glow is now a stepped pixel texture at FLIGHT_ART_SCALE, and the nozzle flame matches the ship's pixel density and warm palette.
The soft-touchdown dust fans out to the sides, so the 'featherlight landing!' payoff shows the whole ship, with sparkles above.
The incident ship pose is clean thanks to the RotSprite pre-rotation, and confetti now emits above the ship.

The audio architecture is robust. The AudioContext is gesture-gated with retry on later gestures and silent degradation. Glue compressor, limiter and clip drive keep the worst-case stack at -3.7 dBFS. Mute plays a short cue before the gain closes, and the context suspends while the tab is hidden.

openIssues: [minor] (audio-fx) The landing thrust plume still reads as a continuous rope or trunk. One orange-to-rust-to-tan column runs from the nozzle and ends in a cream puff 'foot' floating about 40 px above the pad, instead of a flickering jet that breaks up into separate puffs. Landing thrust is the most-seen FX in the landing phase.

[minor] (audio-fx) The incident burst still lacks a clear comic 'poof'. Confetti is sparse (4-5 tiny crosses) and some of it is still buried in the flour at pad level. The flour puffs are partly see-through (a landing leg shows through them) and stack into a vertical column under the ship rather than a ring burst.

[minor] (audio-fx) Flight trail tail puffs are large, flat cream blocks with no shaded rim or outline. Next to the shaded ship they read as bread chunks or toast rather than exhaust smoke, and the biggest puff is roughly as tall as the nozzle housing.

[minor] (audio-fx) Mix balance: ui-hover's momentary loudness is about -40.7 dB, roughly 17 dB under the title music bed (-23 dB). It will be inaudible over music. touchdown-soft (-16.4) is also louder than touchdown-bumpy (-20.9), which inverts the expected impact hierarchy, unless that is an intentional celebration.
[nit] (audio-fx) The stabilizer gyro-star FX could not be visually verified this round. The landing-thrust showcase with S held left the ship out of frame, and no showcase holds the stabilizer.

[nit] (audio-fx) The gallery's R toggle flips relative to the OS preference. With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce emulated, one press of R reported reducedMotion=false, so it is unclear whether the gallery reflects the saved setting or the OS preference.
[nit] (landing) Lantern glows beside the pad are smooth anti-aliased pink radial halos (ADD blend), the same class of non-pixel light the engine glow was just fixed for.

strengths: Huge improvement over baseline: production rabbit portrait, item sprites, memory postcard and parchment card replace the serif placeholder text card entirely; zero fallbacks.

Result copy is outstanding and on-brief: 'a spirited delivery', 'That landing sounded like a cupboard. Very comforting, actually.', '2 friendly bumps along the way', 'landed on try 2 · the moon waited' -- warm, never shaming, backed by a banned-words list in src/data/resultCopy.ts.

Clear visual hierarchy: pixel kicker > display headline > quoted reaction > stamps > mono stats > footer actions; the palette (parchment, ink, terracotta, sage/amber pills) matches design-system.md tokens.

Navigation is explicit: labelled 'back to title [esc]' and 'fly again [enter]' buttons with keycaps; pointer taps only skip the staged reveal; event.repeat is ignored; leave() is guarded against double activation.

Huge leap from the baseline Times-New-Roman text box to a cohesive stationery card: parchment surfaces, design-system state-pill palettes, Silkscreen kicker, Bricolage headline, JetBrains Mono stats. It matches the design-system tokens and 'cozy stationery' intent.

Pixel contract on desktop is now clean. The rabbit portrait, items, stat icons, postcard and stamps all sit on an exact 2x grid with no rotation. Settled frames have no leftover particles (liveTwinkles=0).

Copy is consistently warm and funny, with no shame language. Every outcome reads as a successful delivery ('Reassembled with care. I'll eat it in the order it landed.'), and resultCopyBannedWords is enforced by tests.
Persistence states are surfaced gently and accurately. They cover the session-only footnote for newer-save / storage-unavailable / write-failed and the 'crumpled save, kept a copy' title notice.

openIssues: [minor] (ui (app shell / screens.css) with result builder) In phone portrait the result card (tiny tier) stays live under the DOM rotate overlay, and the CSS sends pointer events through to it. The canvas buttons sit under the overlay card, so a tap on the 'turn your phone sideways' card can invisibly trigger FLY AGAIN or BACK TO TITLE. That breaks the 'navigation only by explicit, visible buttons' rule. It also means the effort put into the tiny tier is never seen.

[minor] (save-results (DeliveryResultScene / resultCopy layouts)) Composition leaves a dead zone in the right column. Under the three stat rows and left of the postcard is an empty parchment block of about 370x100 px on desktop (about 330x110 on compact). The left panel also has empty bands above the portrait and below the item caption. The card reads top-heavy and the postcard looks parked in a corner rather than placed.

[minor] (save-results) Type hierarchy is crowded at the top of the copy column. The quote is bold display type at xl, almost as heavy as the headline, so the two blocks compete. Its greedy wrap also leaves one-word widows ('little gyoza.”', 'landed.”', 'comforting, actually.”'). In the incident state the headline steps down to 2xl, which moves the stamps, divider and stats up about 13 px compared with the other outcomes.

[nit] (save-results / ui kit (Button.ts)) Button language changes between tiers. Desktop uses letter-spaced Silkscreen caps with keycaps. Compact uses lowercase bold Geist with no keycaps and different proportions, so the same screen has two different button identities. The compact footer note also floats with no visual anchor.

[nit] (save-results) On phone landscape the pixel art (rabbit at portraitScale 3, postcard, items) is smooth-downsampled to about 1.6 physical px per art px. It looks soft and slightly blurred next to the crisp desktop rendering. It is acceptable and legible, but not pixel-crisp.

[nit] (save-results (SaveSystem)) When a parseable but malformed save is 'repaired', it is rewritten in place with no backup. Only unparseable or non-object JSON is backed up. A save with unknown or extra fields (e.g. from a newer patch that still says version 1), or with one malformed list, loses that data permanently on first load.

[nit] (save-results) The session-only footnote is italic Geist, which looks like a synthesized oblique. It is the only italic in the UI, and the design system defines no italic role. Small, but a little off-system.

strengths: Environment and prop art (asteroids, tea moon, teahouse, pad, lanterns, rocks, rabbit sprite and portrait, items, UI kit) is cohesive, crisp 2px pixel art with ink outlines and a warm palette that matches colors_and_type.css. It is a large improvement over the baseline.

Landing scene composition (dusk gradient, layered hills, warm teahouse, striped pad) reaches the cozy 'Spiritfarer-lite' bar.

Hero ship fully redrawn at true 64x80 resolution with hard alpha and integer 2x display. Clean dome ring, readable pilot, tapered flame, consistent registration across all 9 frames. It no longer reads as noise next to the asteroids and teahouse.

All 45 manifest entries match exact size and frames. Anchors hold: ground surface at row 8, pad surface at row 6, all sprites reach the bottom row. Provenance is recorded for every folder. Total 545 KB.
All 54 manifest entries exist and match their exact sizes and frame grids, including the RotSprite sheets; there are no fallbacks and no load failures
The lunar-hills-far rework is now readable authored ridges with clean stepped crests; the round-2 smear is gone
The lunar-sky ringed planet is now clean pixel art with a continuous outline and a tidy ring
The nebula is now distinct authored cloud masses with stepped alpha and a warm rim on the plum clouds, instead of blurry mush

openIssues: [minor] (lunar) The baked lunar-sky ringed planet competes with the teahouse, which should be the focal point. It is a huge, saturated orange planet sitting directly behind the orange tiled roof. Its bottom rim is tangent to the roof ridge and chimney, so the two silhouettes merge. It also uses the same full-strength ink outline and saturation as the foreground props, which flattens depth: the sky planet reads as close as the house.

[minor] (asteroids) asteroid-crumb still breaks the asteroid outline language. On its lit upper-left and left edges the silhouette ends in cream or lavender pixels with no dark ink outline, while the right side has one. The lower-left face is still a fairly straight cut. Every other asteroid (rice, sleepy, tea, mochi) has a continuous ink outline.

[minor] (lunar) lunar-hills-far is clean now but tonally flat. The three ridge bands use nearly identical mid-lavenders with little value separation. The foreground band blends into the blue-grey underside of lunar-ground, and the floating crater ellipses add noise without shape. Behind the pad and the teahouse, the hills read as a pale wash rather than layered depth.

[minor] (particles) The flight thrust trail behind the ship reads as separate cream and orange popcorn chunks with hard gaps between them, not a continuous warm puff trail. The large cream lumps are as bright as the gyoza crust and compete with the ship silhouette.
[nit] (space) The teal and slate nebula masses have no rim light and sit very close to the background value, so in flight they read as dark smudges. Only the plum clouds get the warm gold edge.

[nit] (space) stars-far.png has a faint checker dither in its background fill (12 unique colors). It is visible as a fine grid texture at 2x and does not match the flat fill of stars-near and the other dark backgrounds.
[nit] (_probe) The stray art-src/_probe folder (asteroid-72.png, asteroid-probe.png) has no PROVENANCE.md, which breaks the per-folder provenance rule.

usageInvestigation.finding: wave-3 round-3 run (12 agents): 150M cache-read input tokens vs 0.14M output. Agents ran 32-192 turns with contexts growing to 200-260k tokens; every turn re-sends the full context. Context growth was driven by 205 full-size screenshot reads (each ~1.2k tokens that persist for the agent's lifetime), large source-file reads, and long tool output. 12-13 parallel agents exhausted a 5-hour usage window in 5-20 minutes.
mitigations: tools/review_sheet.py: one composite thumbnail sheet per capture run instead of 10-20 full PNG reads; zoomed crops only for details
